objects.title: Lighting for exterior stairs

amendment_ref.note: No amendment to this section is listed in 13VAC5-63-210 section 310.8 (fetched 2026-09-27); the VRC adopts the IRC base.

legal_boundary.statement: Any machine result for this unit is reviewer evidence, not approval. Only the building official's decision under the USBC is lawful approval.

objects.paraphrase: Exterior stairs need a light source at or near the top landing, and basement exterior stairs need light at the bottom landing.

source_links.label: 2021 VRC Chapter 3, section R303.8 (ICC Digital Codes)
2021 IRC Chapter 3 model code (ICC Digital Codes; comparison only)

interpretability.rationale: Q3: exterior stairways need a light source at the top landing, with no light level or location tolerance stated (the interior rule in R303.7 has 1 footcandle). Prince William County lists fixture wattages and distances it will accept, which shows the gap.

ambiguous_terms.issue: Location tolerance and light level are not stated.

candidate_clarification.note: Consider a measurable criterion for exterior stairs like the interior one (a minimum footcandle level at treads and landings) or a stated distance from the top landing.

determinations.citation: Prince William County Building Development, Residential Policy 'Deck Stairway Illumination'
determinations.binding_effect: Local policy for Prince William County only; lists methods the county accepts.
determinations.code_at_issue: IRC as incorporated in the USBC (effective 1997, revised 2019)
determinations.section_at_issue: Exterior stairway illumination (not cited by number)
determinations.holding_summary: The county accepts, as compliant: a 60 W fixture within 5 ft of the top landing; a 150 W flood within 30 ft; or low-voltage fixtures at each step plus one within 3 ft of the bottom step; other methods by letter to the building official.
